steps: Hold both hands flat with fingers together, stacking your dominant hand on top of the other at waist level.
Raise both hands to chest height while separating them outward, keeping the palms facing down as they move.
Rotate your wrists so the palms turn to face each other, finishing with both flat hands held apart at chest level.
tip: Think of opening double doors — the stacked hands part and swing outward.

steps: Make a 'Y' with your dominant hand by extending the thumb and little finger while folding the middle fingers down.
Raise the Y hand to the side of your face, bringing the thumb up beside your mouth with the palm facing you.
Hold the handshape briefly at your cheek, then lower your hand back to a neutral resting position.
tip: The thumb and pinky mimic an old telephone receiver held to your ear and mouth.

steps: Extend the index finger of your dominant hand, folding the remaining fingers into a loose fist.
Touch your chin with the fingertip, keeping the finger pointing upward and the palm facing down.
Flick your hand forward away from your chin so the finger points ahead at chest height.
tip: Words leaving the mouth — the finger taps the chin then shoots forward.

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand flat in front of you at waist level with the palm facing up.
Curve the fingers of your dominant hand into a rounded cupped shape, as if holding a coin.
Bring the cupped hand down from above and tap your fingertips once onto the open palm.
tip: Like dropping a coin into someone's waiting hand.

steps: Hold both hands flat with fingers together in front of your chest, palms facing down.
Move your hands toward each other until your dominant hand comes down to rest on top of the other.
Press the stacked hands down slightly, like closing a lid, then hold them together briefly.
tip: The mirror image of OPEN — instead of parting, the hands come together like a lid shutting.

steps: Raise your dominant hand toward the side of your head with the fingers open and relaxed.
Close your hand into a fist as it reaches your forehead, tapping the knuckles firmly against it.
Keep the back of the fist facing outward with the palm turned toward you as it touches.
tip: Knock on your forehead as if locking the memory inside.

steps: Hold both flat hands in front of your chest with fingers together and palms facing down.
Lift one hand up and place it flat on top of the other, like laying a brick.
Alternate hands, stacking each one on top of the last to build upward layer by layer.
tip: Layer by layer, like a bricklayer — the alternating stack is the whole idea.
